title.en: Volume 33 Biographies 25: She Dishi; Yang Jian; Zhao Gang; Wang Qian; Zhao Chang;Wang Yue; Zhao Wenbiao
title.raw: 卷33 列傳第25 厙狄峙 楊荐 趙剛 王慶 趙昶 王悅 趙文表 Volume 33 Biographies 25: She Dishi; Yang Jian; Zhao Gang; Wang Qian; Zhao Chang;Wang Yue; Zhao Wenbiao

sentences.zh: 厙狄峙 楊荐 趙剛 王慶 趙昶 王悅 趙文表

translations.literal: She Dishi; Yang Jian; Zhao Gang; Wang Qing; Zhao Chang; Wang Yue; Zhao Wenbiao
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of She Dishi, Yang Jian, Zhao Gang, Wang Qing, Zhao Chang, Wang Yue, and Zhao Wenbiao

sentences.zh: 厙狄峙，其先遼東人，本姓段氏，匹磾之後也，因避難改焉。

translations.literal: She Dishi — his forebears were men of Liaodong; originally surnamed Duan, descendants of Pi Di; because of fleeing hardship they changed it.
translations.idiomatic: She Dishi's ancestors came from Liaodong. The clan had originally borne the surname Duan and descended from Pi Di, but changed their name while fleeing calamity.

sentences.zh: 後徙居代，世為豪右。

translations.literal: Later they moved to settle in Dai; generation after generation they were powerful great families.
translations.idiomatic: They later moved to Dai and for generations ranked among the local magnates.

sentences.zh: 祖淩，武威郡守。

translations.literal: Grandfather Ling was Administrator of Wuwei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ling served as administrator of Wuwei commandery.

sentences.zh: 父貞，上洛郡守。

translations.literal: Father Zhen was Administrator of Shangluo commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhen was administrator of Shangluo commandery.

sentences.zh: 峙少以弘厚知名，善騎射，有謀略。

translations.literal: Dishi in youth was known for broad magnanimity; skilled at horsemanship and archery; possessed strategic counsel.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man Dishi was known for his generous temperament; he was a fine rider and archer and had a strategist's mind.

sentences.zh: 仕魏，位高陽郡守。

translations.literal: He served Wei and held the post of Administrator of Gaoyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service under Wei and rose to administrator of Gaoyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 為政仁恕，百姓頗悅之。

translations.literal: In governing he was humane and forgiving; the common people were quite pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was humane and lenient, and the people held him in genuine affection.

sentences.zh: 孝武西遷，峙乃棄官從入關。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Dishi thereupon abandoned office and followed to enter the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu withdrew westward, Dishi resigned his post and followed him through the Pass into Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 大統元年，拜中書舍人，參掌機密，以恭謹見稱。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong, he was appointed Palace Secretariat Attendant; he shared in holding confidential affairs; for respectful prudence he was acclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Datong he was made a palace secretariat attendant, given a share in confidential state business, and won praise for his respectful discretion.

sentences.zh: 遷黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 時與東魏爭衡，戎馬不息，蠕蠕乘虛，屢為邊患。

translations.literal: At the time they vied for mastery with Eastern Wei; war-horses did not cease; Rouran seized the void and repeatedly became a border affliction.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei and the western court were then locked in rivalry, warfare never ceased, and the Rouran took advantage of the opening to raid the frontier again and again.

sentences.zh: 朝議欲結和親，乃使峙往。

translations.literal: Court deliberation wished to conclude marriage alliance; thereupon they sent Dishi to go.
translations.idiomatic: The court resolved to seek a marriage alliance and dispatched Dishi on the mission.

sentences.zh: 峙狀貌魁梧，善於辭令。

translations.literal: Dishi's form and appearance were towering; he excelled at eloquent speech.
translations.idiomatic: Dishi was tall and imposing and gifted in diplomatic speech.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕主雅信重之，自是不復為寇。

translations.literal: The Rouran ruler deeply trusted and honored him; from this they no longer became raiders.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran khan came to trust and esteem him deeply, and from that time they ceased their border raids.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂峙曰：「昔魏絳和戎，見稱前史。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor said to Dishi: "Of old Wei Jiang harmonized the Rong; he was acclaimed in earlier histories.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai told Dishi, "In antiquity Wei Jiang reconciled the Rong tribes and won renown in the histories of the past.

sentences.zh: 以君方之，彼有愧色。

translations.literal: Compared with you, those men would have ashamed faces.
translations.idiomatic: Set beside you, those earlier men would blush with shame.

sentences.zh: 」封高邑縣公，邑八百戶。

translations.literal: " He was enfeoffed Duke of Gaoyi county, fief eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: " He was enfeoffed as duke of Gaoyi county with eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 遷驃騎將軍、岐州刺史，加散騎常侍，增邑二百戶，開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of Fast Cavalry and Inspector of Qi Province, with the added title Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry; his fief was increased by two hundred households; he was granted the bounties of an office equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general of fast cavalry and inspector of Qi Province, made regular attendant of scattered cavalry, given two hundred additional fief households, and granted the privileges of an office equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 恭帝元年，征拜侍中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Gong, he was summoned and appointed Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Gong he was summoned to court and made palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕滅後，突厥強盛，雖與文帝通好，而外連齊氏。

translations.literal: After the Rouran were destroyed, the Turks grew powerful; although they maintained friendly relations with Emperor Wen, outwardly they allied with the house of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the Rouran the Turks rose in strength; though they kept up friendly ties with Yuwen Tai, they also maintained an outward alliance with Qi.

sentences.zh: 太祖又令峙銜命喻之。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor again ordered Dishi to bear the command and instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai again sent Dishi with imperial orders to remonstrate with them.

sentences.zh: 突厥感悟，卽執齊使，歸諸京師。

translations.literal: The Turks were moved to understanding; they immediately seized the Qi envoys and sent them back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks took his words to heart, seized the Qi envoys at once, and sent them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 錄前後功，拜大將軍、安豐郡公，邑通前二千戶。

translations.literal: Recording his services before and after, he was appointed Grand General and Duke of Anfeng commandery, fief in total reaching two thousand households as before.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of his past and recent service he was made grand general and duke of Anfeng commandery, with a combined fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 尋除小司空。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was removed and made Minor Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed minor minister of works.

sentences.zh: 孝閔踐阼，轉小司寇。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, he was transferred to Minor Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin came to the throne he was made minor minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，為都督益潼等三十一州諸軍事、益州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign, he became Area Commander of the military affairs of thirty-one provinces including Yi and Tong, and Inspector of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Shizong's reign he was made area commander over the military affairs of thirty-one provinces including Yi and Tong, and inspector of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 峙性寬和，尚清靜，甚為夷獠所安。

translations.literal: Dishi's nature was broad and mild; he valued quiet purity; the Yi and Liao peoples were greatly settled by him.
translations.idiomatic: Dishi was even-tempered and fond of quiet governance, and the tribal peoples of the region found deep reassurance under his rule.

sentences.zh: 保定四年，除

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Baoding, he was appointed
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding year 4 he was made

translations.literal: (Xuan) [emended: Yi]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: Yi]

sentences.zh: 〔宜〕州刺史。

translations.literal: Governor of 〔Yi〕 Province.
translations.idiomatic: governor of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 天和三年，入為少師。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhe, he entered court and became Junior Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianhe he was recalled to court and made junior preceptor.

sentences.zh: 峙以年老，表乞骸骨，手詔許之。

translations.literal: Dishi, because of old age, memorialized begging to retire; an imperial letter in the emperor's own hand granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Dishi, feeling the weight of his years, submitted a memorial asking to retire; the emperor answered with a personal edict granting his request.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year.

sentences.zh: 贈同州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given the post of Inspector of Tong Province.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously made inspector of Tong Province.

sentences.zh: 諡曰定。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous name Ding.

sentences.zh: 子嶷嗣。

translations.literal: His son Ni succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ni succeeded to his rank.

sentences.zh: 少知名，起家吏部上士。

translations.literal: In youth he was known; he began his career as Senior Clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Ni was known from youth and entered service as a senior clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 歷小內史、小納言，授開府階，遷職方中大夫，為蔡州刺史。

translations.literal: He passed through Junior Palace Secretary and Junior Remonstrance Officer, was granted the rank of an office equal to the Three Excellencies, was transferred to Central Director in the Bureau of Appointments, and became Inspector of Cai Province.
translations.idiomatic: He served as junior palace secretary and junior remonstrance officer, received the rank of an office equal to the Three Excellencies, rose to central director in the Bureau of Appointments, and was made inspector of Cai Province.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died while holding office.

sentences.zh: 子授嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shou succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shou succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 楊荐字承略，秦郡寧夷人也。

translations.literal: Yang Jian, styled Chenglüe, was a native of Ningyi in Qin commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian, courtesy name Chenglüe, came from Ningyi in Qin commandery.

sentences.zh: 父寶，昌平郡守。

translations.literal: His father Bao was Administrator of Changping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bao served as administrator of Changping commandery.

sentences.zh: 荐幼孤，早有名譽。

translations.literal: Jian lost his father in childhood; early on he had reputation and fame.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was orphaned young but early won a name for himself.

sentences.zh: 性廉謹，喜怒不形於色。

translations.literal: His nature was incorrupt and prudent; joy and anger did not appear on his face.
translations.idiomatic: He was upright and cautious by nature, and neither pleasure nor anger showed in his countenance.

sentences.zh: 魏永安中，隨爾朱天光入關討羣賊，封高邑縣男。

translations.literal: In the Yongan period of Wei, he followed Erzhu Tianguang into the Pass to suppress bandits and was enfeoffed Baron of Gaoyi county.
translations.idiomatic: During Wei's Yongan era he followed Erzhu Tianguang through the Pass to suppress rebels and was enfeoffed baron of Gaoyi county.

sentences.zh: 文帝臨夏州，補帳內都督。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen took charge at Xia Province, Jian was appointed adjutant within the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Tai assumed command at Xia Province, Jian was made an adjutant in his personal staff.

sentences.zh: 及平侯莫陳悅，使荐入洛陽請事。

translations.literal: When Houmochen Yue was pacified, Emperor Wen sent Jian into Luoyang to report affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat of Houmochen Yue, Yuwen Tai sent Jian to Luoyang to report on affairs.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武帝授文帝關西大行臺，仍除荐直閤將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Wei appointed Emperor Wen Grand Field Secretariat of the Western Pass; he still removed Jian and made him General of the Direct Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu of Wei appointed Yuwen Tai grand field secretariat of the Western Pass and at the same time made Jian general of the direct guard.

sentences.zh: 時馮翊長公主嫠居，孝武意欲歸諸文帝，乃令武衛元毘喻旨。

translations.literal: At the time the Princess of Fengyi, widowed, lived alone; Emperor Xiaowu wished to give her in marriage to Emperor Wen; thereupon he ordered Military Guard Yuan Pi to convey the intent.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Fengyi was then living in widowhood, and Emperor Xiaowu wished to give her to Yuwen Tai in marriage; he therefore had Military Guard Yuan Pi convey his intent.

sentences.zh: 荐歸白，文帝又遣荐入洛陽請之。

translations.literal: Jian returned and reported; Emperor Wen again sent Jian into Luoyang to request her.
translations.idiomatic: Jian returned and reported back; Yuwen Tai then sent him again to Luoyang to ask for her hand.

sentences.zh: 孝武卽許焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu immediately granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu at once consented.

sentences.zh: 孝武欲向關中，荐贊成其計。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu wished to move toward Guanzhong; Jian supported and accomplished his plan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu resolved to withdraw into Guanzhong, Jian helped bring the plan to fruition.

sentences.zh: 孝武曰：「卿歸語行臺迎我。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu said: "You return and tell the Field Secretariat to come receive me.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu said, "Go back and tell the field secretariat to come and fetch me.

sentences.zh: 」文帝又遣荐與長史宇文測出關候接。

translations.literal: " Emperor Wen again sent Jian together with Chief Clerk Yuwen Ce out of the Pass to await and receive him.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuwen Tai then sent Jian with chief clerk Yuwen Ce through the Pass to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 孝武至長安，進爵清水縣子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu reached Chang'an, Jian was advanced in rank to Viscount of Qingshui county.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaowu reached Chang'an, Jian was promoted to viscount of Qingshui county.

sentences.zh: 魏大統元年，蠕蠕請和親。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong of Wei, Rouran requested marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wei's Datong era the Rouran sought a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 文帝遣荐與楊寬使，幷結婚而還。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen sent Jian together with Yang Kuan as envoys; together they concluded the marriage and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai sent Jian with Yang Kuan as envoys; they concluded the marriage and returned together.

sentences.zh: 進爵為侯。

translations.literal: He was advanced in rank to Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to marquis.

sentences.zh: 又使荐納幣於蠕蠕。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen again sent Jian to deliver betrothal gifts to the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai again sent Jian to the Rouran to present betrothal gifts.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝郁久閭后崩，文帝遣僕射趙善使蠕蠕更請婚。

translations.literal: When Empress Yujiulü of Emperor Wen of Wei died, Emperor Wen sent Vice Director Zhao Shan as envoy to the Rouran to request marriage again.
translations.idiomatic: After the death of Empress Yujiulü, Yuwen Tai sent vice director Zhao Shan to the Rouran to renew the marriage request.

sentences.zh: 善至夏州，聞蠕蠕貳於東魏，欲執使者。

translations.literal: When Shan reached Xia Province, he heard the Rouran were duplicitous toward Eastern Wei and intended to seize the envoys.
translations.idiomatic: When Shan reached Xia Province he learned that the Rouran had turned toward Eastern Wei and meant to seize the envoys.

sentences.zh: 善懼，乃還。

translations.literal: Shan was afraid; thereupon he returned.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing for his life, Shan turned back.

sentences.zh: 文帝乃使荐往，賜黃金十斤、雜彩三百疋。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen thereupon sent Jian to go; he was granted ten catties of gold and three hundred bolts of mixed silks.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai then sent Jian in his place, granting him ten catties of gold and three hundred bolts of mixed silks.

sentences.zh: 荐至蠕蠕，責其背惠食言，幷論結婚之意。

translations.literal: When Jian reached the Rouran, he reproached them for turning their backs on kindness and eating their words; together he set forth the intent of the marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian reached the Rouran he rebuked them for betraying past kindness and breaking their word, and laid out once more the purpose of the marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕感悟，乃遣使隨荐報命焉。

translations.literal: The Rouran were moved to understanding; thereupon they sent envoys to follow Jian and report back.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran took his words to heart and sent envoys back with him to report to the court.

sentences.zh: 及侯景來附，文帝令荐與鎮遏。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing came over in submission, Emperor Wen ordered Jian to garrison and restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing defected to the western court, Yuwen Tai ordered Jian to garrison the area and keep him in check.

sentences.zh: 荐知景翻覆，遂求還，具陳事實。

translations.literal: Jian knew Jing was fickle and treacherous; thereupon he requested to return and fully set forth the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Jian saw that Hou Jing was treacherous and unreliable, asked to be recalled, and laid out the facts in full.

sentences.zh: 文帝乃遣使密追助景之兵。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen thereupon sent envoys in secret pursuit of the troops aiding Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai then secretly sent envoys to recall the troops supporting Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 尋而景叛。

translations.literal: Before long Jing rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Hou Jing rebelled.

sentences.zh: 十六年，大軍東討。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, the great army campaigned east.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year the main army marched east on campaign.

sentences.zh: 文帝恐蠕蠕乘虛寇掠，乃遣荐往更論和好，以安慰之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen feared the Rouran would seize the void to raid and plunder; thereupon he sent Jian to go again to discuss friendly relations, to comfort and reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the Rouran would exploit the opening to raid while the army was away, Yuwen Tai sent Jian again to renew friendly relations and reassure them.

sentences.zh: 進使持節、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，加侍中。

translations.literal: He was promoted envoy bearing the staff, Grand General of Fast Cavalry, and the bounties of an office equal to the Three Excellencies; Palace Attendant was added.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to envoy bearing the staff, grand general of fast cavalry, and the privileges of an office equal to the Three Excellencies, with the added title of palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，除御伯大夫，進爵姚谷縣公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, he was appointed Grand Master of the Imperial Clan; he was advanced in rank to Duke of Yaogu county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin came to the throne he was made grand master of the imperial clan and promoted to duke of Yaogu county.

sentences.zh: 仍使突厥結婚。

translations.literal: He was still sent to the Turks to conclude marriage.
translations.idiomatic: He was again sent to the Turks to arrange a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 突厥可汗弟地頭可汗阿史那庫頭居東面，與齊通和，說其兄欲背先約。

translations.literal: The younger brother of the Turk khan, the Eastern Tegin Ashina Kutou, dwelt in the east; he maintained friendly relations with Qi and persuaded his elder brother to turn against the earlier agreement.
translations.idiomatic: The khan's younger brother, the eastern tegin Ashina Kutou, held the east and was on friendly terms with Qi; he urged his brother to break the prior pact.

sentences.zh: 計謀已定，將以荐等送齊。

translations.literal: The plot was already settled; they intended to send Jian and the others to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was already fixed: Jian and his party were to be handed over to Qi.

sentences.zh: 荐知其意，乃正色責之，辭氣慷慨，涕泗橫流。

translations.literal: Jian knew their intent; thereupon with stern countenance he reproached them; his words were impassioned, tears and mucus streaming down.
translations.idiomatic: Reading their intent, Jian rebuked them to their faces with fierce dignity, his voice ringing with passion until tears streamed down his cheeks.

sentences.zh: 可汗慘然良久曰：「幸無所疑，當共平東賊，然後發遣我女。

translations.literal: The khan, deeply grieved, after a long while said: "Fortunately there is nothing to doubt; we shall together pacify the eastern rebels, and afterward I will send off my daughter.
translations.idiomatic: The khan, visibly shaken, was silent a long while, then said, "Put your doubts aside—we will join forces against the eastern enemy, and only then will I send my daughter on her way.

sentences.zh: 」乃令荐先報命，仍請東討。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he ordered Jian first to report back; still he requested an eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: " He had Jian return with the reply first and asked that an eastern expedition be launched.

sentences.zh: 以奉使稱旨，遷大將軍。

translations.literal: Because in bearing the mission he answered the imperial intent, he was transferred to Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: For fulfilling the imperial commission so ably he was promoted to grand general.

sentences.zh: 保定四年，又納幣於突厥。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Baoding, he again delivered betrothal gifts to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding year 4 he again went to the Turks to present betrothal gifts.

sentences.zh: 還，行小司馬，又行大司徒。

translations.literal: On returning, he acted as Minor Minister of War; he also acted as Grand Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: After his return he served concurrently as minor minister of war and grand minister of education.

sentences.zh: 從陳公純等逆女於突厥，進爵南安郡公。

translations.literal: Following Duke of Chen Chun and the others, he went to receive the bride from the Turks; he was advanced in rank to Duke of Nan'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Duke of Chen Chun and others to fetch the bride from the Turks and was promoted to duke of Nan'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 天和三年，遷總管、梁州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhe, he was transferred to Area Commander and Inspector of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianhe he was made area commander and inspector of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 後以疾卒。

translations.literal: Later he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He later died of illness.

sentences.zh: 趙剛字僧慶，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Gang, styled Sengqing, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gang, courtesy name Sengqing, came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 曾祖蔚，魏幷州刺史。

translations.literal: Great-grandfather Wei was Inspector of Bing Province under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Wei had served Wei as inspector of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 祖寧，高平太守。

translations.literal: Grandfather Ning was Administrator of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ning was administrator of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 父和，太平中，陵江將軍，南討度淮，聞父喪，輒還。

translations.literal: Father He, in the Taiping period, was General Who Crosses the Yangtze; south campaigning he crossed the Huai; hearing of his father's death, he immediately returned.
translations.idiomatic: His father He, during the Taiping era, was general who crosses the Yangtze; while campaigning south of the Huai he heard of his father's death and turned back at once.

sentences.zh: 所司將致之於法，和曰：「罔極之恩，終天莫報。

translations.literal: The office in charge was about to bring him to law; He said: "The boundless grace of a parent — all one's life one cannot repay it.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities were about to punish him, but He said, "A parent's boundless grace can never be repaid in a lifetime.

sentences.zh: 若許安厝，禮畢而卽罪戮，死且無恨。

translations.literal: If you permit me to bury him in peace, when the rites are complete I will immediately accept punishment and execution; even in death I shall have no regret.
translations.idiomatic: If you allow me to bury him properly, I will submit to punishment the moment the rites are done, and go to my death without regret.

sentences.zh: 」言訖號慟，悲感傍人。

translations.literal: When his words ended he wailed and sobbed; grief moved those beside him.
translations.idiomatic: He finished speaking and broke into wailing sobs that moved all who stood near.

sentences.zh: 主司以聞，遂宥之。

translations.literal: The chief official reported it; thereupon they pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The chief official reported the matter, and he was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 喪畢，除寧遠將軍。

translations.literal: When mourning was complete, he was appointed General of Distant Pacification.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he was made general of distant pacification.

sentences.zh: 大統初，追贈右將軍、膠州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, posthumously he was given the posts of General of the Right and Inspector of Jiao Province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Datong era he was posthumously made general of the right and inspector of Jiao Province.

sentences.zh: 剛少機辯，有幹能。

translations.literal: Gang in youth was quick-witted in debate and possessed practical ability.
translations.idiomatic: Gang was quick-witted and capable from youth.

sentences.zh: 起家奉朝請。

translations.literal: He began his career as Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as attendant at court.

sentences.zh: 累遷鎮東將軍、銀青光祿大夫，歷大行臺郎中、征東將軍，加金紫階，領司徒府從事中郎，加閤內都督。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotions he became General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master with the Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon; he passed through Grand Field Secretariat Director, General Who Campaigns East, with the added gold-and-purple rank, headed Attendant Gentleman in the Ministry of Education, and was added Inner Headquarters Adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to general who pacifies the east and grand master with the silver seal and blue ribbon, served as director in the grand field secretariat and general who campaigns east, received the gold-and-purple rank, became attendant gentleman in the Ministry of Education, and was made inner headquarters adjutant.

sentences.zh: 及魏孝武與齊神武構隙，剛密奉旨召東荊州刺史馮景昭率兵赴闕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei and Gao Huan fell into enmity, Gang secretly received the edict and summoned Eastern Jing Province Inspector Feng Jingzhao to lead troops to rush to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei and Gao Huan fell out, Gang secretly received orders to summon Feng Jingzhao, inspector of Eastern Jing Province, to lead troops to the capital.

sentences.zh: 未及發，而神武已逼洛陽，孝武西遷。

translations.literal: Before they could set out, Divine Martial had already pressed upon Luoyang, and Emperor Xiaowu moved west.
translations.idiomatic: Before they could march, Gao Huan had already closed on Luoyang and Emperor Xiaowu withdrew westward.

sentences.zh: 景昭集府僚文武，議其去就。

translations.literal: Jingzhao assembled the civil and military officials of the prefecture to discuss whether to stay or go.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao gathered his civil and military staff to debate their course.

sentences.zh: 司馬馮道和請據州待北方處分。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator Feng Daohe requested holding the province and awaiting disposition from the north.
translations.idiomatic: Chief administrator Feng Daohe urged holding the province and waiting for orders from the north.

sentences.zh: 剛曰：「公宜勒兵赴行在所。

translations.literal: Gang said: "Your lordship ought to muster troops and proceed to the imperial residence.
translations.idiomatic: Gang said, "Your lordship should muster troops and go to the emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 」久之更無言者。

translations.literal: " For a long while no one else spoke.
translations.idiomatic: " A long silence followed.

sentences.zh: 剛抽刀投地曰：「公若為忠臣，可斬道和；

translations.literal: Gang drew his sword and cast it to the ground, saying: "If your lordship would be a loyal minister, you may cut down Daohe;
translations.idiomatic: Gang drew his sword, threw it to the ground, and said, "If you mean to stay loyal, strike Daohe down;

sentences.zh: 如欲從賊，可見殺。

translations.literal: if you wish to follow the rebel, you may kill me.
translations.idiomatic: if you mean to follow the rebel, kill me instead.

sentences.zh: 」景昭感悟，遂率衆赴關右。

translations.literal: " Jingzhao was moved to understanding and thereupon led his forces west of the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: " Jingzhao took his point and led his men west of the Pass.

sentences.zh: 屬侯景逼穰城，東荊州人楊祖歡等起兵應景，以其衆邀景昭於路。

translations.literal: Just then Hou Jing pressed on Xiangcheng; Yang Zuhuan of Eastern Jing Province and others raised troops to answer Jing and with their forces intercepted Jingzhao on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Hou Jing pressed Xiangcheng; Yang Zuhuan of Eastern Jing and others rose for Hou Jing and waylaid Jingzhao on the road.

sentences.zh: 景昭戰敗，剛遂沒於蠻。

translations.literal: Jingzhao was defeated in battle; Gang thereupon fell into barbarian hands.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao was beaten in battle and Gang fell into barbarian hands.

sentences.zh: 後自贖免。

translations.literal: Later he ransomed himself and was released.
translations.idiomatic: He later ransomed himself and went free.

sentences.zh: 乃見東魏東荊州刺史李魔憐，勸令歸關西。

translations.literal: He then saw Eastern Wei Eastern Jing Province Inspector Li Molian and urged him to return allegiance to the west.
translations.idiomatic: He then saw Li Molian, Eastern Wei inspector of Eastern Jing, and urged him to return to the western court.

sentences.zh: 魔憐納之，使剛至幷州密觀事勢。

translations.literal: Molian accepted it and sent Gang to Bing Province to observe affairs in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Molian agreed and sent Gang to Bing Province to watch affairs in secret.

sentences.zh: 神武引剛內宴，因令剛齎書申勅荊州。

translations.literal: Divine Martial invited Gang to an inner feast and ordered him to carry letters conveying imperial commands to Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan entertained Gang at a private banquet and had him carry letters with imperial orders to Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 剛還報魔憐，仍說魔憐斬祖歡等，以州歸西。

translations.literal: Gang returned and reported to Molian; he still urged Molian to execute Zu Huan and the others and surrender the province to the west.
translations.idiomatic: Gang returned to Molian and again urged him to execute Zu Huan and the others and surrender the province to the west.

sentences.zh: 魔憐乃使剛入朝。

translations.literal: Molian thereupon sent Gang to court.
translations.idiomatic: Molian then sent Gang to court.

sentences.zh: 大統初，剛於霸上見太祖，具陳關東情實。

translations.literal: Early in Datong, at Bashang Gang saw Grand Progenitor and set forth in full the realities of affairs east of the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Datong, at Bashang, Gang saw Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai and laid out in full what was happening east of the Pass.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉之，封陽邑縣子，邑三百戶，除車騎將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor commended him; he was enfeoffed Viscount of Yangyi county, fief three hundred households, and appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai praised him, enfeoffed him as viscount of Yangyi with three hundred households, and made him general of chariots and cavalry and left grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 論復東荊州功，進爵臨汝縣伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: For merit in recovering Eastern Jing Province, he was advanced to Baron of Linru county, fief five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For recovering Eastern Jing Province he was promoted to baron of Linru with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 初，賀拔勝、獨孤信以孝武西遷之後，並流寓江左。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Heba Sheng and Dugu Xin, after Emperor Xiaowu's move west, both sojourned in the Yangtze region.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaowu withdrew west, Heba Sheng and Dugu Xin had both been living in exile south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 至是剛言於魏文帝，請追而復之。

translations.literal: At this time Gang spoke to Emperor Wen of Wei and requested that they be recalled and restored.
translations.idiomatic: Gang now asked Emperor Wen of Wei to recall them and restore them to service.

sentences.zh: 乃以剛為兼給事黃門侍郎，使梁魏興，齎移書與其梁州刺史杜懷寶等論鄰好，幷致請勝等移書。

translations.literal: Thereupon Gang was appointed Concurrent Supervisor in the Attendant-in-Ordinary's Office at the Yellow Gate and sent to Liang's Wei Xing, bearing letters to its Liang Province Inspector Du Huaibao and others to discuss neighborly friendship, and also to deliver the request letters concerning Sheng and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Gang was made concurrent supervisor in the attendant-in-ordinary's office at the Yellow Gate and sent to Liang's Wei Xing with letters to Liang inspector Du Huaibao and others on neighborly relations, and with the request to return Sheng and the others.

sentences.zh: 寶卽與剛盟歃，受移赴建康，仍遣行人隨剛報命。

translations.literal: Huaibao immediately entered alliance oath with Gang, received the letters and proceeded to Jiankang, and still sent an envoy with Gang to report back.
translations.idiomatic: Huaibao at once swore alliance with Gang, took the letters to Jiankang, and sent an envoy back with Gang to report.

sentences.zh: 是年，又詔剛使三荊，聽在所便宜從事。

translations.literal: That year, an edict again ordered Gang to mission to the three Jings, with discretion to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: That year an edict again sent Gang on mission to the three Jing regions with authority to act as local conditions required.

sentences.zh: 使還，稱旨，進爵武城縣侯，除大丞相府帳內都督。

translations.literal: When the mission returned and met the imperial intent, he was advanced to Marquis of Wucheng county and appointed adjutant within the headquarters of the Grand Chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned with the mission and satisfied the court, he was promoted to marquis of Wucheng and made adjutant in the grand chancellor's personal staff.

sentences.zh: 復使魏興，重申前命。

translations.literal: He was again sent to Wei Xing to renew the prior orders.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent again to Wei Xing to renew the earlier orders.

sentences.zh: 尋而梁人禮送賀拔勝、獨孤信等。

translations.literal: Before long the men of Liang respectfully sent off Heba Sheng, Dugu Xin, and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Liang courteously sent Heba Sheng, Dugu Xin, and the others on their way.

sentences.zh: 頃之，御史中尉董紹進策，請圖梁漢。

translations.literal: Before long, Censor-in-Chief Dong Shao submitted a plan requesting a campaign against Liang's Han region.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward censor-in-chief Dong Shao submitted a plan to strike Liang's Han region.

sentences.zh: 以紹為行臺、梁州刺史，率士馬向漢中。

translations.literal: Shao was made Mobile Headquarters and Inspector of Liang Province, leading soldiers and horses toward Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was made mobile headquarters commissioner and inspector of Liang Province and led troops toward Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 剛以為不可，而朝議已決，遂出軍。

translations.literal: Gang judged it impossible, but court deliberation had already been decided; thereupon the army set out.
translations.idiomatic: Gang thought the plan unsound, but the court had already decided; the army marched anyway.

sentences.zh: 詔竟無功而還，免為庶人。

translations.literal: By edict they ultimately returned without achievement; Shao was removed and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: The expedition returned without success by imperial order, and Shao was stripped of rank and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 除剛潁川郡守，加通直散騎常侍、衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Gang was appointed Administrator of Yingchuan commandery, with the added titles Direct Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and Guard Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Gang was made administrator of Yingchuan, with the added titles direct regular attendant of scattered cavalry and guard grand general.

sentences.zh: 從復弘農。

translations.literal: He followed in the recovery of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in recovering Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 進拜大都督、東道軍司，節度開府李延孫等七軍，攻復陽城，擒太守王智納。

translations.literal: He was advanced and appointed Grand Area Commander and Eastern Route Army Secretary, coordinating seven armies including Opener of the Way Li Yansun and others; they attacked and recovered Yangcheng and captured Administrator Wang Zhina.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand area commander and eastern-route army secretary, put in command of seven armies including Li Yansun's, retook Yangcheng, and captured administrator Wang Zhina.

sentences.zh: 轉陳留郡守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Administrator of Chenliu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to administrator of Chenliu commandery.

sentences.zh: 東魏行臺吉寧率衆三萬攻陷郡城，剛突出，還保潁川，重行郡事。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei's Mobile Headquarters Ji Ning led thirty thousand troops, attacked and captured the commandery seat; Gang broke out, returned to hold Yingchuan, and again performed commandery duties.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei mobile headquarters commissioner Ji Ning took thirty thousand men, captured the commandery seat, and Gang broke out, fell back on Yingchuan, and resumed commandery duties.

sentences.zh: 復為侯景所破，乃率餘衆赴洛陽。

translations.literal: He was again defeated by Hou Jing; thereupon he led his remaining troops to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing defeated him again, and he led his survivors to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 大行臺元海遣剛還郡徵糧。

translations.literal: Grand Mobile Headquarters Yuan Hai sent Gang back to the commandery to levy grain.
translations.idiomatic: Grand mobile headquarters commissioner Yuan Hai sent Gang back to the commandery to levy grain.

sentences.zh: 時景衆已入潁川，剛於西界招復陽翟二萬戶，轉輸送洛。

translations.literal: At that time Jing's forces had already entered Yingchuan; at the western border Gang recovered twenty thousand households of Yangdi and transported provisions to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: By then Hou Jing's troops had entered Yingchuan; on the western border Gang rallied twenty thousand households at Yangdi and shipped provisions to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 明年，洛陽不守。

translations.literal: The next year Luoyang could not be held.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Luoyang fell.

sentences.zh: 剛遠隔敵中，連戰破東魏廣州刺史李仲侃。

translations.literal: Gang, far separated within enemy territory, repeatedly fought and defeated Eastern Wei Guang Province Inspector Li Zhongkan.
translations.idiomatic: Cut off deep in enemy country, Gang fought again and again and defeated Eastern Wei Guang inspector Li Zhongkan.

sentences.zh: 時侯景別帥陸太、潁川郡守高沖等衆八千人，寇襄城等五郡。

translations.literal: At the time Hou Jing's secondary commander Lu Tai, Yingchuan Administrator Gao Chong, and others with eight thousand troops raided five commanderies including Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Hou Jing's lieutenant Lu Tai, Yingchuan administrator Gao Chong, and others with eight thousand men raided five commanderies including Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 剛簡步騎五百，大破沖等。

translations.literal: Gang selected five hundred foot and horse and thoroughly routed Chong and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Gang picked five hundred infantry and cavalry and routed Gao Chong and his force.

sentences.zh: 開府李延孫為長史楊伯簡所害，剛擊斬之。

translations.literal: Opener of the Way Li Yansun was killed by Chief Clerk Yang Bojian; Gang struck and executed Bojian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yansun was murdered by his chief clerk Yang Bojian; Gang attacked and killed Bojian.

sentences.zh: 又攻拔廣州，進軍陽翟。

translations.literal: He again attacked and took Guang Province and advanced to Yangdi.
translations.idiomatic: He took Guang Province again and advanced on Yangdi.

sentences.zh: 侯景自鄴入魯陽，與剛接戰。

translations.literal: Hou Jing entered Luyang from Ye and joined battle with Gang.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing came from Ye into Luyang and gave battle to Gang.

sentences.zh: 旬有三日，旋軍宜陽。

translations.literal: For thirteen days they fought; then he turned the army toward Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: They fought for thirteen days; then Gang withdrew toward Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 時河南城邑，一彼一此。

translations.literal: At the time the cities and towns of Henan were divided—now one side, now the other.
translations.idiomatic: Henan's towns and cities were then divided between the two sides.

sentences.zh: 剛復出軍伊、洛，侯景亦度河築城。

translations.literal: Gang again led troops out in the Yi and Luo region; Hou Jing also crossed the river and built fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: Gang campaigned again along the Yi and Luo; Hou Jing also crossed the river and built forts.

sentences.zh: 剛前後下景三郡，獲郡守一人，別破其行臺梅遷，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: Gang before and after reduced three of Jing's commanderies, captured one commandery administrator, and separately broke Jing's Mobile Headquarters Mei Qian, taking heads numbering more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In repeated operations Gang took three of Hou Jing's commanderies, captured one administrator, and separately routed Hou Jing's mobile headquarters under Mei Qian, taking more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 除尚書金部郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed Secretary in the Gold Bureau of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was made secretary in the gold bureau of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 高仲密以北豫州來附，兼大行臺左丞，持節赴潁川節度義軍。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhongmi came over with North Yuzhou in submission, Gang was concurrently made Left Assistant of the Grand Mobile Headquarters, bearing the staff to go to Yingchuan and coordinate the righteous armies.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhongmi defected with North Yuzhou, Gang was concurrently made left assistant of the grand mobile headquarters, bore the staff to Yingchuan, and coordinated the loyalist forces.

sentences.zh: 師還，剛別破侯景前驅于南陸，復獲其郡守二人。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Gang separately defeated Hou Jing's vanguard at Nanlu and again captured two of his commandery administrators.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return Gang separately routed Hou Jing's vanguard at Nanlu and captured two more commandery administrators.

sentences.zh: 時有流言傳剛東叛，齊神武因設反間，聲遣迎接。

translations.literal: At the time slander circulated that Gang had rebelled to the east; Qi Divine Martial accordingly set up a stratagem, publicly announcing he would send men to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors then spread that Gang had gone over to the east; Gao Huan set a counterplot and openly announced he would send men to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 剛乃率騎襲其下塢，拔之，露板言狀。

translations.literal: Gang thereupon led cavalry to raid their lower stockade, took it, and posted a proclamation setting forth the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Gang led cavalry against their lower stockade, took it, and posted a public notice explaining what had happened.

sentences.zh: 太祖知剛無貳，乃加賞賚焉。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor knew Gang had no disloyalty and thereupon added rewards and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai knew Gang was loyal and added rewards and gifts.

sentences.zh: 除營州刺史，進爵為公，增邑二百戶，加大都督、車騎大將軍、儀同三司、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Inspector of Ying Province, advanced in rank to duke, given two hundred additional fief households, and made Grand Area Commander, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, and Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was made inspector of Ying Province, promoted to duke with two hundred additional fief households, and given the titles grand area commander, grand general of chariots and cavalry, equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, and regular attendant of scattered cavalry.

translations.literal: (Cao) [emended: Ying]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: Ying]

sentences.zh: 〔渭〕州民鄭五醜構逆，與叛羌傍乞鐵匆相應，令剛往鎮之。

translations.literal: The people of 〔Wei〕 Province — Zheng Wuchou plotted rebellion and responded together with the rebel Qiang Pangqi Tiecong; Gang was ordered to go and garrison the region.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Wei Province, led by Zheng Wuchou, rebelled in concert with the rebel Qiang Pangqi Tiecong, Gang was ordered to go and pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 將發，魏文帝引見內寢，舉觴屬剛曰：「昔侯景在東，為卿所困。

translations.literal: About to set out, Emperor Wen of Wei received him in audience in the inner chambers, raised a cup and entrusted Gang, saying: "Formerly Hou Jing in the east was hemmed in by you.
translations.idiomatic: Before he set out, Emperor Wen of Wei received him in the inner chambers, raised a cup, and told him, "You once had Hou Jing trapped in the east.

sentences.zh: 黠羌小豎，豈足勞卿謀慮也。

translations.literal: These crafty Qiang striplings — how could they be worth troubling your counsel?
translations.idiomatic: These crafty Qiang upstarts are hardly worth your strategic attention.

sentences.zh: 」時五醜已剋定夷鎮，所在立柵。

translations.literal: " At that time Wuchou had already taken Yizhen; everywhere stockades were erected.
translations.idiomatic: " By then Wuchou had already taken Yizhen and stockades had gone up everywhere.

sentences.zh: 剛至，竝攻破之，散其黨與。

translations.literal: When Gang arrived, he broke them all, and dispersed their followers.
translations.idiomatic: When Gang arrived he stormed them one after another and broke up their bands.

sentences.zh: 五醜於是西奔鐵怱。

translations.literal: Wuchou thereupon fled west to Tiecong.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchou then fled west to Tiecong.

sentences.zh: 剛又進破鐵匆偽廣寧郡。

translations.literal: Gang again advanced and defeated Tiecong's false Guangning commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Gang advanced again and destroyed Tiecong's puppet Guangning commandery.

sentences.zh: 屬宇文貴等西討，詔以剛行渭州事，資給糧餼。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Gui and others campaigned west, an edict had Gang act as governor of Wei Province affairs and supply grain and provisions.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Gui and others marched west, an edict put Gang in charge of Wei Province affairs and supplied his grain and provisions.

sentences.zh: 鐵匆平，所獲羌卒千人，配剛軍中，教以戎旅，皆盡其力用。

translations.literal: When Tiecong was pacified, a thousand Qiang captives taken were assigned to Gang's army; taught in military formation, all exerted their strength to the full.
translations.idiomatic: After Tiecong was pacified, a thousand Qiang captives were assigned to Gang's army; drilled in military service, all gave their full strength.

sentences.zh: 加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，入為光祿卿。

translations.literal: He was given the added titles Grand General of Fast Cavalry and Opener of the Way Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, and entered court as Minister of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He received the added titles grand general of fast cavalry and opener of the way equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, and entered court as minister of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 六官建，拜膳部中大夫。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed Grand Master in the Food Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were established he was made grand master in the Food Bureau.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，進爵浮陽郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, he was advanced to Duke of Fuyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin came to the throne he was promoted to duke of Fuyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 出為利州總管、利沙方渠四州諸軍事。

translations.literal: He went out as Area Commander of Li, with military authority over four provinces including Li, Sha, Fang, and Qu.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as area commander of Li, with military authority over Li, Sha, Fang, and Qu provinces.

sentences.zh: 沙州氐恃險逆命，剛再討服之。

translations.literal: The Di of Sha Province relied on terrain and defied orders; Gang twice campaigned and subdued them.
translations.idiomatic: The Di of Sha Province relied on difficult terrain and defied orders; Gang subdued them in two campaigns.

sentences.zh: 方州生獠自此始從賦役。

translations.literal: The raw Liao of Fang Province from this time began to submit to taxation and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the raw Liao of Fang Province began to accept taxation and corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 剛以偽信州濱江負阻，遠連殊俗，蠻左強獷，曆世不賓，乃表請討之。

translations.literal: Gang, because false Xin Province bordered the river and relied on barriers, far connected to exotic peoples, with fierce and unruly tribal peoples on the left who for generations had not submitted, memorialized requesting a punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Gang, finding that the puppet Xin Province lay on the river behind natural barriers, linked to distant tribes, and held fierce tribal peoples who had never submitted for generations, memorialized asking to campaign against it.

sentences.zh: 詔剛率利沙等十四州兵，兼督儀同十人、馬步一萬往經略焉。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Gang to lead troops of fourteen provinces including Li and Sha, concurrently supervising ten officers equal to the Three Excellencies and ten thousand horse and foot, to go and manage affairs there.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Gang to lead troops from fourteen provinces including Li and Sha, with ten officers equal to the Three Excellencies and ten thousand horse and foot under his command, to pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 仍加授渠州刺史。

translations.literal: He was additionally given the post of Inspector of Qu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made inspector of Qu Province.

sentences.zh: 剛初至，渠帥憚其軍威，相次降款。

translations.literal: When Gang first arrived, the Qu chieftains feared his military might and one after another submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Gang first arrived the Qu chieftains feared his army and surrendered one after another.

sentences.zh: 後以剛師出踰年，士卒疲弊，尋復亡叛。

translations.literal: Later, because Gang's army had been out more than a year, the soldiers were worn and spent; soon they again fled and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Later, with his army in the field more than a year, the troops grew exhausted; soon they deserted and rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 後遂以無功而還。

translations.literal: In the end they returned without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he returned without success.

sentences.zh: 又與所部儀同尹才失和，被徵赴闕。

translations.literal: He also fell out with Yi Cai, an officer equal to the Three Excellencies under his command, and was summoned to court.
translations.idiomatic: He also quarreled with Yi Cai, one of his officers equal to the Three Excellencies, and was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 遇疾，卒於路。

translations.literal: He met with illness and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill on the way and died on the road.

sentences.zh: 年五十七。

translations.literal: He was fifty-seven years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made

translations.literal: (Zhong) [emended: Zhong]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: Zhong]

sentences.zh: 〔中〕淅涿三州刺史。

translations.literal: Inspector of the three provinces 〔Zhong〕, Xi, and Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: inspector of the three provinces Zhong, Xi, and Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 諡曰成。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous name Cheng.

sentences.zh: 子元卿嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yuanqing succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanqing succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 王慶字興慶，太原祁人也。

translations.literal: Wang Qing, styled Xingqing, was a native of Qi in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qing, courtesy name Xingqing, came from Qi in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 父因，魏靈州刺史、懷德縣公。

translations.literal: Father Yin was Inspector of Ling Province under Wei and Duke of Huaide county.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yin had served Wei as inspector of Ling Province and duke of Huaide county.

sentences.zh: 初，突厥與周和親，許納女為后。

translations.literal: At first the Turks and Zhou were allied by marriage; they promised to give a daughter as empress.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Turks and Northern Zhou were allied by marriage, and the Turks had promised a daughter as empress.

sentences.zh: 而齊人知之，懼成合從之勢，亦遣使求婚，財饋甚厚。

translations.literal: When the men of Qi learned of it, fearing formation of a joint alliance, they too sent envoys to seek marriage, with very generous gifts of wealth.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi learned of this, fearing a joint alliance, it too sent envoys to seek marriage with lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 突厥貪其重賂，便許之。

translations.literal: The Turks, greedy for their heavy bribes, at once agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks, coveting the rich bribes, agreed at once.

sentences.zh: 朝議以魏氏昔與蠕蠕結婚，遂為齊人離貳。

translations.literal: Court deliberation noted that the Wei house formerly had married the Rouran, and the men of Qi had thus divided and estranged them.
translations.idiomatic: The court recalled that the Wei had once married the Rouran and that Qi had exploited the breach to divide them.

sentences.zh: 今者復恐改變，欲遣使結之。

translations.literal: Now again they feared a change of heart and wished to send envoys to bind them.
translations.idiomatic: Now they feared another change and wished to send envoys to bind the Turks.

sentences.zh: 遂授慶左武伯，副楊荐為使。

translations.literal: Thereupon Qing was appointed Left Military Chief and deputy to Yang Jian as envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Qing was therefore made left military chief and sent as deputy to Yang Jian on the mission.

sentences.zh: 是歲，遂興入幷之役。

translations.literal: That year they launched the campaign to enter Bing.
translations.idiomatic: That year the court launched the campaign into Bing.

sentences.zh: 慶乃引突厥騎，與隨公楊忠至太原而還。

translations.literal: Qing thereupon led Turk cavalry, and with Duke of Sui Yang Zhong reached Taiyuan and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Qing led Turk cavalry and, with Duke of Sui Yang Zhong, reached Taiyuan and returned.

sentences.zh: 以齊人許送皇姑及世母，朝廷遂與通和。

translations.literal: Because the men of Qi promised to send the emperor's paternal aunt and the empress dowager, the court thereupon entered communication and peace with them.
translations.idiomatic: Because Qi promised to send back the emperor's paternal aunt and the empress dowager, the court opened peace talks with Qi.

sentences.zh: 突厥聞之，復致疑阻，於是又遣慶往喻之。

translations.literal: The Turks heard of it, again raised suspicion and obstruction; thereupon Qing was again sent to instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks heard of this, grew suspicious and obstructive again, and Qing was sent once more to explain.

sentences.zh: 可汗感悅，結好如初。

translations.literal: The khan was moved and pleased; friendly relations were restored as before.
translations.idiomatic: The khan was pleased and moved; friendly relations were restored as before.

sentences.zh: 五年，復與宇文貴使突厥逆女。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he again went with Yuwen Gui as envoy to the Turks to escort the bride back.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he again went with Yuwen Gui as envoy to the Turks to escort the bride home.

sentences.zh: 自此，以慶信著北蕃，頻歲出使。

translations.literal: From then on, because of Qing's trustworthiness he became renowned among the northern frontier peoples, and year after year he went on embassy.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Wang Qing's reliability made him famous on the northern frontier, and he was sent on embassy year after year.

sentences.zh: 後更至突厥，屬其可汗暴殂，突厥謂慶曰：「前後使來，逢我國喪者，皆剺面表哀。

translations.literal: Later when he again reached the Turks, it happened that their khan died suddenly. The Turks said to Qing: "Envoys who came before, whenever they met with our national mourning, all gashed their faces to show grief.
translations.idiomatic: When he later returned to the Turks, their khan had died suddenly. The Turks told Qing, "Earlier envoys who came during our national mourning all gashed their faces to show grief.

sentences.zh: 況今二國和親，豈得不行此事。

translations.literal: Now that the two states are allied by marriage, how can this not be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Now that our two states are allied by marriage, how can you refuse to do the same?"

sentences.zh: 」慶抗辭不從，突厥見其守正，卒不敢逼。

translations.literal: " Qing firmly refused on principle. Seeing that he held to what was right, the Turks in the end did not dare press him.
translations.idiomatic: " Qing stood firm and refused. Seeing that he would not bend, the Turks in the end did not dare force him.

sentences.zh: 武帝聞而嘉之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu heard of it and commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu heard of it and praised him.

sentences.zh: 錄慶前後使功，遷開府儀同三司、兵部大夫，進爵為公。

translations.literal: Recording Qing's merits on his successive embassies, he was promoted to opener of the Way with the Three Precedences and grandee of the Ministry of War, and advanced in rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: The court recorded Qing's service on his successive embassies and promoted him to opener of the Way with the Three Precedences and grandee of the Ministry of War, raising him to duke.

sentences.zh: 歷丹、中二州刺史。

translations.literal: He served as governor of Dan and Zhong prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Dan and Zhong prefectures in succession.

sentences.zh: 為政嚴肅，吏不敢欺。

translations.literal: In government he was stern and dignified, and officials did not dare deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with stern dignity, and his subordinates did not dare cheat him.

sentences.zh: 大象元年，授小司徒，加上大將軍、總管汾石二州五鎮諸軍事、汾州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daxiang, he was appointed junior minister of education, given the added ranks of senior grand general and area commander of military affairs for Fen and Shi prefectures and five garrisons, and made governor of Fen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daxiang he was made junior minister of education, given the added titles of senior grand general and area commander of military affairs for Fen and Shi prefectures and five garrisons, and appointed governor of Fen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 又除延州總管，進位柱國。

translations.literal: He was also appointed area commander of Yan Province and advanced to pillar of state.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made area commander of Yan Province and raised to pillar of state.

sentences.zh: 開皇元年，進爵平昌郡公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang, he was advanced to Duke of Pingchang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaihuang he was raised to Duke of Pingchang commandery.

sentences.zh: 卒於鎮。

translations.literal: He died at his garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He died while holding his post.

sentences.zh: 贈上柱國，諡曰莊。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given senior pillar-of-state rank, and his posthumous title was Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made senior pillar of state and given the posthumous title Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子淹嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 趙昶字長舒，天水南安人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Chang, styled Changshu, was a native of Nan'an in Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chang, courtesy name Changshu, came from Nan'an in Tianshui commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖襄，仕魏至中山郡守，因家於代。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xiang served Wei as governor of Zhongshan commandery and settled his family in Dai.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xiang served Wei as governor of Zhongshan commandery and settled the family in Dai.

sentences.zh: 祖泓，廣武令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hong was magistrate of Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hong was magistrate of Guangwu county.

sentences.zh: 父琛，上洛郡守。

translations.literal: His father Chen was governor of Shangluo commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chen had governed Shangluo commandery.

sentences.zh: 昶少聰敏，有志節。

translations.literal: Chang from youth was clever and keen, and had resolve and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Zhao Chang was clever and keen, with firm resolve and integrity.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，以材力聞。

translations.literal: At weak crown he was known for talent and strength.
translations.idiomatic: Once he came of age he was known for talent and physical prowess.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，起家拜都督，鎮小平津。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era he entered office and was appointed commander, garrisoning Xiaoping Ford.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiaochang era he entered office as a commander and was posted to garrison Xiaoping Ford.

sentences.zh: 魏北中郎將高千甚敬重之。

translations.literal: Northern Wei's General of the Center Army Gao Qian greatly respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Qian, Northern Wei's general of the center army, held him in great esteem.

sentences.zh: 千牧兗州，以昶行臨渙、北梁二郡事。

translations.literal: When Qian governed Yan Province, he had Chang act in the affairs of Linhuan and Beiliang commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Qian governed Yan Province, he put Chang in charge of Linhuan and Beiliang commanderies.

sentences.zh: 大統初，千還鎮陝，又以昶為長史、中軍都督。

translations.literal: At the start of Datong, when Qian returned to garrison Shaan, he again made Chang chief clerk and central army commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Datong, when Gao Qian returned to garrison Shaan, he again made Chang his chief clerk and central army commander.

sentences.zh: 太祖平弘農，擢為相府典簽。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor pacified Hongnong, Chang was promoted to records officer of the chancellor's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai pacified Hongnong, Chang was promoted to records officer of the chancellor's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 大統九年，大軍失律於邙山，清水氐酋李鼠仁自軍逃還，憑險作亂。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Datong, the great army lost discipline at Mount Mang; Qingshui Di chieftain Li Shuren fled back from the army and, relying on rugged terrain, raised rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Datong the main army was routed at Mount Mang; Qingshui Di chieftain Li Shuren deserted and, holding difficult ground, rebelled.

sentences.zh: 隴右大都督獨孤信頻遣軍擊之，不克。

translations.literal: Great governor-general of Longyou Dugu Xin repeatedly sent troops to attack him but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Xin, great governor-general of Longyou, repeatedly sent troops against him but could not defeat him.

sentences.zh: 太祖將討之，欲先遣觀其勢。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor was about to campaign against him and wished first to send someone to observe their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai planned to campaign against him and wanted first to send someone to assess the enemy's strength.

sentences.zh: 顧問誰可為。

translations.literal: He asked whom he could send.
translations.idiomatic: He asked who could go.

sentences.zh: 左右莫對。

translations.literal: Those at his side none answered.
translations.idiomatic: No one around him spoke up.

sentences.zh: 昶曰：「此小豎爾，以公威，孰不聽命。

translations.literal: Chang said: "This petty fellow — with your authority, who would not obey?"
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "This petty upstart — with your authority, who would dare refuse?"

sentences.zh: 」太祖壯之，遂令昶使焉。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor admired his spirit and thereupon ordered Chang to go as envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai admired his boldness and sent Chang as envoy.

sentences.zh: 昶見鼠仁，喻以禍福。

translations.literal: Chang saw Shuren and explained to him the consequences of fortune and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Chang met Li Shuren and explained the consequences of submission and rebellion.

sentences.zh: 羣凶聚議，或從或否。

translations.literal: The ringleaders gathered to discuss; some agreed, some refused.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leaders met to discuss the matter; some agreed, some refused.

sentences.zh: 其逆命者，復將加刃於昶。

translations.literal: Those who resisted were again about to put blades to Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Those who resisted were again about to kill Chang.

sentences.zh: 而昶神色自若，志氣彌厲。

translations.literal: Yet Chang's expression remained calm, and his spirit grew fiercer still.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Chang remained calm in face and spirit, and his resolve only hardened.

sentences.zh: 鼠仁感悟，遂相率降。

translations.literal: Shuren was moved to understanding and thereupon led his followers in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shuren was moved and led his followers in surrender.

sentences.zh: 氐梁道顯叛，攻南由。

translations.literal: Di chieftain Liang Daoxian rebelled and attacked Nanyou.
translations.idiomatic: The Di chieftain Liang Daoxian rebelled and attacked Nanyou.

sentences.zh: 太祖復遣昶慰諭之，道顯等皆卽款附。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor again sent Chang to reassure and instruct them, and Daoxian and the others at once submitted in good faith.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai again sent Chang to reassure them, and Daoxian and the others submitted at once.

sentences.zh: 東秦州刺史魏光因徙其豪帥四十餘人幷部落於華州，太祖卽以昶為都督領之。

translations.literal: Eastern Qin Province inspector Wei Guang had moved more than forty tribal chiefs together with their clans to Hua Province; the Grand Progenitor thereupon made Chang commander to lead them.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Qin Province inspector Wei Guang had moved more than forty tribal chiefs and their clans to Hua Province; Yuwen Tai then made Chang commander over them.

sentences.zh: 先是，汾州胡叛，再遣昶慰勞之，皆知其虛實。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Hu of Fen Province rebelled, Chang had twice been sent to comfort and reward them, and all came to know their true strength and situation.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Hu of Fen Province rebelled, Chang had twice been sent to comfort them, so he knew their real strength and disposition.

sentences.zh: 及大軍往討，昶為先驅，遂破之。

translations.literal: When the great army went to punish them, Chang served as vanguard and thereupon broke them.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army marched to suppress them, Chang led the van and routed them.

sentences.zh: 以功封章武縣伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Zhangwu county with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was enfeoffed Baron of Zhangwu county with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 十五年，拜安夷郡守，帶長虵鎮將。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed governor of Anyi commandery with concurrent command of Chang'ao Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was made governor of Anyi commandery and concurrently commander of Chang'ao Garrison.

sentences.zh: 氐族荒獷，世號難治，昶威懷以禮，莫不悅服。

translations.literal: The Di clans were wild and fierce; generation after generation they were called hard to govern. Chang won them by authority and kindness through ritual, and none failed to submit gladly.
translations.idiomatic: The Di were wild and fierce and had long been considered hard to govern; Zhao Chang won them with authority and kindness, and all submitted gladly.

sentences.zh: 期歲之後，樂從軍者千餘人。

translations.literal: After a year, more than a thousand willingly joined military service.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year more than a thousand men willingly joined the army.

sentences.zh: 加授帥都督。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally made commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時屬軍機，科發切急，氐情難之，復相率謀叛。

translations.literal: At the time military affairs pressed urgently, and conscription demands were severe; the Di found it hard to bear and again gathered to plot rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Military demands were pressing and conscription was severe; the Di found it unbearable and again plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 昶又潛遣誘說，離間其情，因其攜貳，遂輕往臨之。

translations.literal: Chang again secretly sent men to win them over and drive wedges among them; exploiting their divided loyalties, he then went lightly to face them in person.
translations.idiomatic: Chang again sent secret envoys to win men over and sow division; when their loyalties split, he went in person with only a light escort.

sentences.zh: 羣氐不知所為，咸來見昶。

translations.literal: The Di masses did not know what to do and all came to see Chang.
translations.idiomatic: The Di did not know what to do and all came to see Zhao Chang.

sentences.zh: 乃收其首逆者二十餘人斬之，餘衆遂定。

translations.literal: He then seized more than twenty ringleaders and beheaded them, and the rest of the multitude was thereupon settled.
translations.idiomatic: He then seized more than twenty ringleaders and executed them, and the rest of the people settled down.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉之，除大都督，行南秦州事。

translations.literal: The court commended him and appointed him great commander acting in the affairs of Southern Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: The court commended him and made him great commander with acting authority over Southern Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 時氐帥蓋鬧等反，昶復討擒之。

translations.literal: At the time the Di chieftain Gai Nao and others rebelled; Chang again campaigned against them and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Di chieftain Gai Nao and others rebelled, Chang campaigned against them again and captured them.

sentences.zh: 進撫軍將軍，加通直散騎常侍，又與史寧破宕昌羌、獠二十餘萬。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army, given the added rank of regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, and together with Shi Ning broke more than two hundred thousand Dangchang Qiang and Liao.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general who pacifies the army, given the added rank of regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, and with Shi Ning defeated more than two hundred thousand Dangchang Qiang and Liao.

sentences.zh: 拜武州刺史、車騎大將軍、儀同三司、諸州軍事。

translations.literal: He was appointed governor of Wu Province, chariot-and-horse grand general, opener of the Way with the Three Precedences, and commander of military affairs for the prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was made governor of Wu Province, chariot-and-horse grand general, opener of the Way with the Three Precedences, and commander of military affairs for the prefectures.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝初，加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gong of Wei, he was given the added ranks of swift-cavalry grand general and opener of the Way with the Three Precedences.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Emperor Gong of Wei's reign he was given the added ranks of swift-cavalry grand general and opener of the Way with the Three Precedences.

sentences.zh: 潭水羌叛，殺武陵、潭水二郡守。

translations.literal: The Tanshui Qiang rebelled and killed the governors of Wuling and Tanshui commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Tanshui Qiang rose in revolt and slew the governors of Wuling and Tanshui.

sentences.zh: 昶率儀同駱天义等騎步五千討平之。

translations.literal: Chang led opener-of-the-way Luo Tianyi and others with five thousand cavalry and infantry to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Chang led Luo Tianyi and other openers of the way with five thousand cavalry and infantry to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，鳳州人仇周貢、魏興等反，自號周公，有衆八千人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong, the men of Feng Province, Qiu Zhougong and Wei Xing, rebelled, styled themselves Duke Zhou, and had a following of eight thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Emperor Shizong's reign, Qiu Zhougong and Wei Xing of Feng Province rebelled, styled themselves Duke Zhou, and mustered eight thousand followers.

sentences.zh: 破廣化郡，攻沒諸縣，分兵西入，圍廣業、修城二郡。

translations.literal: They broke Guanghua commandery, captured and overran the counties, sent detachments westward, and besieged Guangye and Xiucheng commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: They overran Guanghua commandery, seized the counties, sent detachments west, and besieged Guangye and Xiucheng commanderies.

sentences.zh: 廣業郡守薛爽、修城郡守杜杲等請昶為援。

translations.literal: Guangye commandery governor Xue Shuang and Xiucheng commandery governor Du Guo and others asked Chang for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Guangye governor Xue Shuang, Xiucheng governor Du Guo, and others asked Zhao Chang for relief.

sentences.zh: 昶遣使報杲，為周貢党樊伏興等所獲。

translations.literal: Chang sent an envoy to reply to Guo, but the envoy was captured by Zhougong's partisan Fan Fuxing and others.
translations.idiomatic: Chang sent an envoy to answer Du Guo, but Fan Fuxing and other Zhougong partisans captured him.

sentences.zh: 興等知昶將至，解修城圍，據泥功嶺，設六伏以待昶。

translations.literal: Fuxing and the others, knowing Chang was about to arrive, lifted the siege of Xiucheng, took position on Nigong Ridge, and set six ambushes to await Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Chang was coming, Fan Fuxing and his men lifted the siege of Xiucheng, held Nigong Ridge, and laid six ambushes for him.

sentences.zh: 昶至，遂遇其伏，合戰，破之。

translations.literal: When Chang arrived, he thereupon met their ambush; they joined battle and he broke them.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang arrived he walked into the ambush, fought, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 廣業之圍亦解。

translations.literal: The siege of Guangye was also lifted.
translations.idiomatic: The siege of Guangye was lifted as well.

sentences.zh: 昶追之至泥陽川而還。

translations.literal: Chang pursued them to Niyang River and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Chang pursued them to the Niyang River and then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 興州人段吒及氐酋薑多復反，攻沒郡縣，昶討斬之。

translations.literal: The men of Xing Province, Duan Tuo, and the Di chieftain Jiang Duo again rebelled, captured and overran commanderies and counties; Chang campaigned against them and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Tuo of Xing Province and the Di chieftain Jiang Duo rebelled again, overran commanderies and counties, and were suppressed and beheaded by Chang.

sentences.zh: 語在《氐傳》。

translations.literal: The account is in the Biography of the Di.
translations.idiomatic: The account is given in the Biography of the Di.

sentences.zh: 昶自以被拔擢居將帥之任，傾心下士。

translations.literal: Chang, judging himself promoted and placed in a commander's post, devoted his heart to men below him.
translations.idiomatic: Having been raised to command, Zhao Chang devoted himself wholeheartedly to the men under him.

sentences.zh: 虜獲氐、羌，撫而使之，皆為昶盡力。

translations.literal: Captured Di and Qiang he treated kindly and put to use, and all exerted themselves fully for Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Captured Di and Qiang he treated kindly and employed, and all fought their hardest for him.

sentences.zh: 太祖常曰：「不煩國家士馬而能威服氐、羌者，趙昶有之矣。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor often said: "Without troubling the state's soldiers and horses yet able to awe and subdue the Di and Qiang — Zhao Chang has this."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai often said, "Without costing the state soldiers and horses, yet able to awe the Di and Qiang into submission — only Zhao Chang can do that."

sentences.zh: 」至是，世宗錄前後功，進爵長道郡公，賜姓宇文氏，賞勞甚厚。

translations.literal: At this time Emperor Shizong recorded his past and present merits, advanced him to Duke of Changdao commandery, granted him the surname Yuwen, and rewarded and honored him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: At this point Emperor Shizong recorded his past and present service, raised him to Duke of Changdao commandery, granted him the surname Yuwen, and rewarded him lavishly.

sentences.zh: 二年，徵拜賓部中大夫，行吏部。

translations.literal: In the second year he was summoned and appointed grandee of the Guest Department, acting in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was summoned to court as grandee of the Guest Department with acting authority in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 尋以疾卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died of illness.

sentences.zh: 王悅字衆喜，京兆藍田人也。

translations.literal: Wang Yue, styled Zhongxi, was a native of Lantian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue, courtesy name Zhongxi, came from Lantian in Jingzhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 少有氣幹，為州里所稱。

translations.literal: From youth he had force of character and was praised in his district.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he had force of character and was respected in his home district.

sentences.zh: 魏永安中，爾朱天光西討，引悅為其府騎兵參軍，除石安令。

translations.literal: In the Yongan era of Wei, when Erzhu Tianguang campaigned west, he recruited Yue as cavalry adjutant in his headquarters and appointed him magistrate of Shi'an.
translations.idiomatic: During Wei's Yongan era, when Erzhu Tianguang marched west, he recruited Wang Yue as cavalry adjutant in his headquarters and made him magistrate of Shi'an county.

sentences.zh: 十三年，侯景據河南來附，仍請兵為援。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Hou Jing held Henan and came over in submission, still requesting troops as relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Hou Jing held Henan and submitted to the court, still asking for troops as reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 太祖先遣韋法保、賀蘭願德等帥衆助之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor first sent Wei Fabao, Helan Yuande, and others to lead troops to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai first sent Wei Fabao, Helan Yuande, and others to lead troops to his aid.

sentences.zh: 悅言於太祖曰：「侯景之於高歡，始則篤鄉黨之情，末乃定君臣之契，位居上將，職重台司，論其分義，有同魚水。

translations.literal: Yue said to the Grand Progenitor: "Hou Jing's relation to Gao Huan at first was the warm affection of fellow townsmen; in the end it became a lord-and-subject bond. He held the highest general's rank and the weightiest office at court; in share of duty and right they were like fish and water.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue told Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, "Hou Jing's tie to Gao Huan began as the warm affection of fellow townsmen and ended as a true lord-and-subject bond. He held the highest general's rank and the weightiest court office; in duty and trust they were like fish and water.

sentences.zh: 今歡始死，景便離貳。

translations.literal: Now that Huan has just died, Jing at once turned disloyal.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Huan has just died, Jing has already turned disloyal.

sentences.zh: 豈不知君臣之道有虧，忠義之禮不足？

translations.literal: Does he not know that the way of lord and subject has been breached and the rites of loyalty and righteousness are insufficient?"
translations.idiomatic: Does he not see that the bond between lord and subject is broken and the rites of loyalty and righteousness count for nothing?"

sentences.zh: 蓋其所圖旣大，不恤小嫌。

translations.literal: It is simply that his designs are already grand and he does not worry over small affronts.
translations.idiomatic: It is simply that his ambitions are already vast and he does not care about lesser slights.

sentences.zh: 然尚能背德於高氏，豈肯盡節於朝廷。
