translations.literal: Yet if he can break faith with the Gao clan, how would he loyally exhaust himself for the court?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet if he can betray the Gao clan, how would he serve the court with full loyalty?"

sentences.zh: 今若益之以勢，援之以兵，非唯侯景不為池中之物，亦恐朝廷貽笑將來也。

translations.literal: If we now add power to his position and reinforce him with troops, not only will Hou Jing not remain a fish in a pond — the court may also become a laughingstock for generations to come."
translations.idiomatic: If we now strengthen his position and reinforce him with troops, Hou Jing will not stay a fish in a pond — and the court may become a laughingstock for generations to come."

sentences.zh: 」太祖納之，乃遣行臺郎中趙士憲追法保等，而景尋叛。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor accepted his advice and thereupon sent mobile headquarters bureau director Zhao Shixian to recall Fabao and the others, and Jing soon rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai accepted his counsel and sent mobile headquarters bureau director Zhao Shixian to recall Fabao and the others; Hou Jing rebelled soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 十四年，授雍州大中正、帥都督，加衛將軍、右光祿大夫、都督。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed chief rectifier of Yong Province and commander-in-chief, given the added ranks of guard general, right grandee for shining virtue, and commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was made chief rectifier of Yong Province and commander-in-chief, with the added ranks of guard general, right grandee for shining virtue, and commander.

sentences.zh: 率所部兵從大將軍楊忠征隨郡、安陸，竝平之。

translations.literal: He led his troops following Grand General Yang Zhong in campaigning against Sui and Anlu commanderies, and both were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He led his troops under Grand General Yang Zhong in the campaign against Sui and Anlu commanderies and helped pacify both.

sentences.zh: 時懸兵深入，悅支度路程，勒其部伍，節減糧食。

translations.literal: At the time the army was deep in hostile territory; Yue calculated routes, kept the ranks in order, and rationed provisions.
translations.idiomatic: The army was deep in enemy country; Wang Yue calculated routes, kept the ranks in order, and rationed provisions.

sentences.zh: 及至竟陵，諸軍多有匱乏，悅出稟米六百石分給之。

translations.literal: When they reached Jingling, many of the armies were short of supplies; Yue issued six hundred shi of ration rice and distributed it among them.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Jingling many units were short of supplies; Yue issued six hundred shi of ration rice and shared it among them.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞而嘉焉。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor heard of it and commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai heard of it and praised him.

sentences.zh: 尋拜京兆郡守，加使持節、車騎大將軍、儀同三司、散騎常侍，遷大行臺尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed governor of Jingzhao commandery, given bearer of the staff, chariot-and-horse grand general, opener of the Way with the Three Precedences, and regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, and transferred to grand secretary of the great mobile headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made governor of Jingzhao commandery, given bearer of the staff, chariot-and-horse grand general, opener of the Way with the Three Precedences, and regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, and transferred to grand secretary of the great mobile headquarters.

sentences.zh: 又領所部兵從達奚武征梁漢。

translations.literal: He again led his troops following Daxi Wu in campaigning against Liang Han.
translations.idiomatic: He again led his troops under Daxi Wu in the campaign against Liang Han.

sentences.zh: 軍出，武令悅說其城主楊賢。

translations.literal: When the army set out, Wu ordered Yue to persuade the city commander Yang Xian.
translations.idiomatic: When the army marched out, Daxi Wu ordered Wang Yue to persuade the city commander Yang Xian.

sentences.zh: 悅乃貽之書曰：「夫惟德是輔，天道之常也；

translations.literal: Yue then sent him a letter saying: "He who is aided by virtue — that is Heaven's constant way;
translations.idiomatic: Yue then sent him a letter saying, "He whom virtue assists follows Heaven's constant way;

sentences.zh: 見機而作，人事之會也。

translations.literal: To act when the moment appears — that is the human occasion for success.
translations.idiomatic: to act when the moment appears is the human occasion for success.

sentences.zh: 梁主內虧刑政，外闕藩籬。

translations.literal: The Liang ruler is deficient within in law and punishment, and lacks without the barriers of frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang ruler is deficient within in law and punishment and lacks without the barriers of frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 匹夫攘袂，舉國傾覆。

translations.literal: One common man flings up his sleeves, and the whole state is overturned.
translations.idiomatic: A single commoner can raise his sleeves and overturn the realm.

sentences.zh: 非直下民離心，抑亦上玄所棄。

translations.literal: It is not only that the people below have lost heart — Heaven on high has cast the realm aside as well.
translations.idiomatic: It is not only that the people below have lost heart — Heaven above has cast the realm aside as well.

sentences.zh: 我相公膺千齡之運，創三分之業，道洽區中，威振方外。

translations.literal: Our prime minister has received the fortune of a thousand ages, founded the enterprise of tripartite division; his Way pervades the central realm, and his authority shakes the outer lands.
translations.idiomatic: Our prime minister has embraced fortune a thousand years in the making and founded the tripartite enterprise; his Way fills the realm, and his authority resounds beyond the borders.

sentences.zh: 聲教所被，風行草偃；

translations.literal: Where his civilizing instruction reaches, the wind blows and grass bends;
translations.idiomatic: Where his teaching spreads, the grass bends before the wind;

sentences.zh: 兵車所指，雲除霧廓。

translations.literal: Where his chariots and armies point, clouds are cleared and mists swept away.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever his armies march, clouds clear and mists are swept away.

sentences.zh: 斯固天下所共聞，無俟二談也。

translations.literal: This is indeed what all under Heaven have heard together; there is no need to discuss it twice.
translations.idiomatic: All under Heaven has heard this already; there is no need to rehearse it again.

sentences.zh: 大將軍高陽公，韞韜略之秘，總熊羆之旅，受脤廟堂，威懷巴漢。

translations.literal: Great General Duke of Gaoyang harbors hidden stratagems, commands troops like bears and panthers, received sacrificial meat in the ancestral temple, and with authority wins over Ba and Han.
translations.idiomatic: Great General Daxi Wu, Duke of Gaoyang, holds hidden stratagems close, commands armies like bears and panthers, took sacrificial commission in the ancestral temple, and has awed and won over Ba and Han.

sentences.zh: 先附者必賞，後服者必誅。

translations.literal: Those who submit first will surely be rewarded; those who submit late will surely be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Those who submit first will be rewarded; those who submit late will be punished.

sentences.zh: 君兵糧旣寡，救援路絕。

translations.literal: Your troops and grain are already few; the route for relief is cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Your troops and supplies are already depleted, and relief cannot reach you.

sentences.zh: 欲守，則城池無縈帶之險；

translations.literal: If you wish to defend, the city-walls lack the protection of winding waters;
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to hold out, your walls lack moats and natural barriers;

sentences.zh: 欲戰，則士卒有土崩之勢。

translations.literal: If you wish to fight, the soldiers have the momentum of earth crumbling.
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to fight, your soldiers are on the brink of collapse.

sentences.zh: 以此求安，未見其可。

translations.literal: To seek safety on this basis — one does not see how it is possible.
translations.idiomatic: To seek safety on such terms is to chase the impossible.

sentences.zh: 昔韓信背項，前典以為美談；

translations.literal: Formerly Han Xin turned against Xiang Yu; the earlier classics hold this up as fine talk;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Han Xin abandoned Xiang Yu, and the classics praise it as wise action;

sentences.zh: 黃權歸魏，良史稱其盛烈。

translations.literal: Huang Quan went over to Wei; good historians praised his magnificent achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Quan submitted to Wei, and good historians praised his heroic choice.

sentences.zh: 事有變通，今其則也。

translations.literal: Affairs allow for flexibility; now is the time for that rule.
translations.idiomatic: Circumstances allow change; that rule applies today.

sentences.zh: 」賢於是遂降。

translations.literal: " Xian thereupon submitted.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Yang Xian submitted.

sentences.zh: 悅白武云：「白馬要衝，是必爭之地。

translations.literal: Yue told Wu, saying: "White Horse is a vital thoroughfare; it is ground that must be fought over.
translations.idiomatic: Yue told Daxi Wu, "White Horse is a strategic crossroads and ground both sides must contest.

sentences.zh: 今城守寡弱，易可圖也。

translations.literal: Now the garrison is few and weak; it can easily be taken.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison is now sparse and weak, and the place can easily be seized.

sentences.zh: 若蜀兵更至，攻之實難。

translations.literal: If Shu troops arrive further, attacking it will truly be difficult."
translations.idiomatic: If Shu reinforcements arrive, taking it will truly be difficult."

sentences.zh: 」武然之，令悅率輕騎七百，徑趣白馬。

translations.literal: Wu approved it and ordered Yue to lead seven hundred light cavalry straight to White Horse.
translations.idiomatic: Daxi Wu agreed and ordered Yue to lead seven hundred light horsemen straight to White Horse.

sentences.zh: 悅先示其禍福，其將梁深遂以城降。

translations.literal: Yue first showed them fortune and disaster; their commander Liang Shen thereupon surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yue first set out the consequences for them; the defending commander Liang Shen then surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 梁武陵王紀果遣其將任奇率步騎六千，欲先據白馬。

translations.literal: Liang Prince of Wuling Ji indeed sent his general Ren Qi leading six thousand infantry and cavalry, wishing to seize White Horse first.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Prince of Wuling Ji had indeed sent his general Ren Qi at the head of six thousand infantry and cavalry to seize White Horse first.

sentences.zh: 行次闕城，聞已降，乃還。

translations.literal: When marching they reached Que City; hearing it had already surrendered, they returned.
translations.idiomatic: Marching to Que City, they heard the place had already submitted and turned back.

sentences.zh: 及梁州平，太祖卽以悅行刺史事。

translations.literal: When Liang Prefecture was pacified, the Grand Progenitor immediately had Yue act as governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Prefecture was pacified, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai had Yue act as its governor.

sentences.zh: 招攜初附，民吏安之。

translations.literal: He drew in those newly submitting; officials and commoners were settled.
translations.idiomatic: He drew in those who had just submitted, and officials and people alike were reassured.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝二年，徵還本任。

translations.literal: In the second year of Deposed Emperor of Wei, he was recalled to his original post.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Fei of Wei he was recalled to his former post.

sentences.zh: 屬改行臺為中外府，尚書員廢，以儀同領兵還鄉里。

translations.literal: At the time the mobile headquarters was changed to the Central-and-Outer Directorate; the Secretariat posts were abolished; with equal-in-three-departments rank he led troops back to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the great mobile headquarters became the Central-and-Outer Directorate, Secretariat posts were abolished, and Yue returned home leading troops with equal-in-three-departments rank.

sentences.zh: 悅旣久居顯職，及此之還，私懷怏怏。

translations.literal: Yue had long held conspicuous office; on this return he privately harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Having long held high office, Yue returned in private discontent.

sentences.zh: 猶陵駕鄉里，失宗黨之情。

translations.literal: He still rode roughshod over his home district and lost the goodwill of kin and clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: He still lorded it over his home district and alienated kin and neighbors.

sentences.zh: 其長子康，恃

translations.literal: His eldest son Kang, relying on
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Kang drew on

translations.literal: (Yue) [supplied]
translations.idiomatic: [supplied: Yue]

sentences.zh: 舊望，遂自驕縱。

translations.literal: former standing, thereupon became arrogant and self-indulgent.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue's former standing, grew arrogant and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 所部軍人，將有婚禮，康乃非理淩辱。

translations.literal: Among the troops under his command, one was about to have a wedding; Kang unjustly insulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Among the troops under his command, one soldier was about to marry; Kang humiliated him without cause.

sentences.zh: 軍人訴之。

translations.literal: The soldier appealed.
translations.idiomatic: The soldier appealed against him.

sentences.zh: 悅及康竝坐除名，仍配流遠防。

translations.literal: Yue and Kang were both stripped of office and relegated to distant frontier exile.
translations.idiomatic: Yue and Kang were both dismissed from office and sent into distant frontier exile.

sentences.zh: 及于謹伐江陵，平，悅從軍展效，因留鎮之。

translations.literal: When Yu Jin attacked Jiangling and pacified it, Yue followed the army and displayed merit; he was therefore left to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Jin attacked and took Jiangling, Yue followed the campaign and performed well and was left to garrison the city.

sentences.zh: 孝閔踐阼，依例復官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin acceded, according to precedent he was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin acceded, Yue was restored to office according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 授郢州。

translations.literal: He was given Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He received Ying prefecture.

sentences.zh: 尋拜使持節、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、大都督、司水中大夫，進爵藍田縣侯。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed commissioner with credentials, grand general of agile cavalry, opening-office equal-in-three-departments, great governor-general, and middle grandee of the Water Office; he was advanced to Marquis of Lantian County.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made commissioner with credentials, grand general of agile cavalry, opening-office equal-in-three-departments, great governor-general, and middle grandee of the Water Office, and was raised to Marquis of Lantian County.

sentences.zh: 遷司憲中大夫，賜姓宇文氏，又進爵河北縣公。

translations.literal: He was transferred to middle grandee of the Rectifier Office, granted the surname Yuwen, and further advanced to Duke of Hebei County.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to middle grandee of the Rectifier Office, granted the surname Yuwen, and raised to Duke of Hebei County.

sentences.zh: 悅性儉約，不營生業，雖出入榮顯，家徒四壁而已。

translations.literal: Yue by nature was frugal; he did not pursue profit-making; though he passed in and out of glory, his household had nothing but bare walls.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue was frugal by nature and made no pursuit of profit; though he moved in the highest circles, his household remained bare.

sentences.zh: 世宗手勅勞勉之，賜粟六百石。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong personally wrote an edict to praise and encourage him, and granted six hundred shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong wrote a personal edict to praise and encourage him and granted six hundred shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 保定元年，卒於位。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoding, he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding year 1 he died in office.

sentences.zh: 康嗣。

translations.literal: Kang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Kang succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 官至司邑下大夫。

translations.literal: He reached the office of lower grandee of the Manors Office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to lower grandee of the Manors Office.

sentences.zh: 趙文表，其先天水西人也，後徙居南鄭。

translations.literal: Zhao Wenbiao — his ancestors were natives of western Tianshui; later they moved to settle at Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wenbiao's ancestors came from western Tianshui; the family later moved to Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 累世為二千石。

translations.literal: For generations they served as two-thousand-bushel officials.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the family had served as two-thousand-bushel officials.

sentences.zh: 父江，性方嚴，有度量。

translations.literal: His father Jiang was upright and stern by nature, with breadth of character.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiang was upright and stern by nature and had real breadth of judgment.

sentences.zh: 歷官東巴州刺史、計部中大夫、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、御伯中大夫，封昌國縣伯。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of governor of Eastern Ba Province, middle grandee of the Accounts Office, grand general of agile cavalry, opening-office equal-in-three-departments, and middle grandee of the Charioteer Office; he was enfeoffed as Baron of Changguo County.
translations.idiomatic: He held successive posts as governor of Eastern Ba Province, middle grandee of the Accounts Office, grand general of agile cavalry, opening-office equal-in-three-departments, and middle grandee of the Charioteer Office, and was enfeoffed Baron of Changguo County.

sentences.zh: 贈虞絳二州刺史，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted the posts of inspector of Yu and Jiang Provinces; posthumous name Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made inspector of Yu and Jiang Provinces and given the posthumous name Zhen.

sentences.zh: 文表少而修謹，志存忠節。

translations.literal: Wenbiao in youth was cultivated and careful; his aspiration was fixed on loyalty and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbiao from youth was careful and restrained and set his heart on loyalty and integrity.

sentences.zh: 便弓馬，能左右馳射。

translations.literal: He was adept at bow and horse and could ride and shoot to left and right.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled with bow and horse and could shoot while galloping to either side.

sentences.zh: 好讀《左氏春秋》，略舉大義。

translations.literal: He loved to read Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals and could summarize the main principles.
translations.idiomatic: He loved Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals and could summarize its larger themes.

sentences.zh: 起家為太祖親信。

translations.literal: He began his career as a trusted follower of the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a trusted follower of Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝元年，從開府田弘征山南，以功授都督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei, he followed Kaifu Tian Hong in campaigning south of the mountains; for merit he was granted the rank of governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei he followed Kaifu Tian Hong on the campaign south of the mountains and was made governor for his service.

sentences.zh: 復從平南巴州及信州，遷帥都督。

translations.literal: He again followed in pacifying Southern Ba Prefecture and Xin Prefecture, and was promoted to commanding governor.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed in the pacification of Southern Ba and Xin prefectures and was promoted to commanding governor.

sentences.zh: 又從許國公宇文貴鎮蜀，行昌城郡事。

translations.literal: He again followed Duke of Xu Yuwen Gui in garrisoning Shu, acting as administrator of Changcheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Duke of Xu Yuwen Gui in garrisoning Shu and served as acting administrator of Changcheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 加中軍將軍、左金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was given the added ranks of middle army general and left grand master with golden seal and purple ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He received the added ranks of middle army general and left grand master with golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 保定元年，除許國公府司馬，轉大都督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoding, he was appointed marshal of Duke of Xu's government office and transferred to great governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding year 1 he was made marshal of Duke of Xu Yuwen Gui's government office, then transferred to great governor-general.

sentences.zh: 五年，授畿伯下大夫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was granted lower grandee of the Capital Charioteer Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made lower grandee of the Capital Charioteer Office.

sentences.zh: 又為許國公府長史。

translations.literal: He again served as chief administrator of Duke of Xu's government office.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as chief administrator in the Duke of Xu's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 尋拜車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed grand general of chariots and cavalry and equal-in-three-departments.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made grand general of chariots and cavalry with equal-in-three-departments rank.

sentences.zh: 仍從宇文貴使突厥，迎皇后，進止儀注，皆令文表典之。

translations.literal: He again followed Yuwen Gui as envoy to the Turks to welcome the empress; protocol for advances and halts — all were entrusted to Wenbiao to manage.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Yuwen Gui as envoy to the Turks to welcome the empress, and Wenbiao was put in charge of all protocol for advances and halts.

sentences.zh: 文表斟酌而行，皆合禮度。

translations.literal: Wenbiao adjusted and carried out each step; all accorded with ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbiao judged each step and carried it out, and everything accorded with ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 及皇后將入境，突厥托以馬瘦，行除。

translations.literal: When the empress was about to enter the border, the Turks pleaded that the horses were lean and slowed the march.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress was about to cross the border, the Turks pleaded that the horses were exhausted and slowed the march.

sentences.zh: 文表慮其為變，遂說突厥使羅莫緣曰：「后自發彼藩，已淹時序，途經沙漠，人馬疲勞。

translations.literal: Wenbiao feared they were plotting trouble, and therefore persuaded the Turk envoy Luomoyuan, saying: "Since the empress set out from your frontier, seasons have already passed; the route crossed deserts; men and horses are weary.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbiao feared they meant treachery and persuaded the Turk envoy Luomoyuan, saying, "Since the empress left your frontier, seasons have passed; she has crossed deserts, and men and horses are worn out.

sentences.zh: 且東寇每伺間隙，吐谷渾亦能為變。

translations.literal: Moreover eastern enemies always watch for openings; Tuyuhun too can make trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern enemies always watch for openings, and Tuyuhun too may exploit a crisis.

sentences.zh: 今君以可汗之愛女，結姻上國，曾無防慮，豈人臣之體乎。

translations.literal: Now you, bearing the khan's beloved daughter who has contracted marriage with the superior state, have no precaution at all — is this the conduct of a minister?"
translations.idiomatic: You carry the khan's beloved daughter to marry into the superior state, yet take no precautions — is that the conduct of a loyal minister?"

sentences.zh: 」莫緣然之，遂倍道兼行，數日至甘州。

translations.literal: Luomoyuan agreed; they then doubled the pace by forced marches and in several days reached Gan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Luomoyuan agreed; they pressed on by forced marches and reached Gan Province in a few days.

sentences.zh: 以迎后功，別封伯陽縣伯，邑六百戶。

translations.literal: For the merit of welcoming the empress, he was separately enfeoffed Baron of Boyang County with a fief of six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his service in welcoming the empress he was separately enfeoffed Baron of Boyang County with a fief of six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 天和三年，除梁州總管府長史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhe, he was appointed chief administrator of the Liang Prefecture governor-general's office.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhe year 3 he was made chief administrator of the Liang Prefecture governor-general's office.

sentences.zh: 所管地名恆陵者，方數百里，竝生獠所居，恃其險固，常懷不軌。

translations.literal: Within his jurisdiction was a place called Hengling, several hundred li square, all inhabited by raw Liao; relying on rugged terrain, they constantly harbored rebellious intent.
translations.idiomatic: Within his jurisdiction lay Hengling, several hundred li across, inhabited by raw Liao who relied on the rugged terrain and constantly nursed rebellious designs.

sentences.zh: 文表率衆討平之。

translations.literal: Wenbiao led troops to attack and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbiao led troops against them and pacified the region.

sentences.zh: 遷蓬州刺史，政尚仁恕，夷獠懷之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to governor of Peng Prefecture; in government he favored benevolence and forbearance; the Yi and Liao peoples cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to governor of Peng Prefecture, ruled with benevolence and lenience, and won the affection of Yi and Liao peoples.

sentences.zh: 加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was given the added ranks of grand general of agile cavalry and opening-office equal-in-three-departments.
translations.idiomatic: He received the added ranks of grand general of agile cavalry and opening-office equal-in-three-departments.

sentences.zh: 又進位大將軍，爵為公。

translations.literal: He was further promoted to great general and ennobled as duke.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to great general and was enfeoffed as a duke.

sentences.zh: 大象中，拜吳州總管。

translations.literal: In the Daxiang era, he was appointed governor-general of Wu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daxiang era he was made governor-general of Wu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時開府于顗為吳州刺史。

translations.literal: At that time Kaifu Yu Yan was governor of Wu Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Kaifu Yu Yan was governor of Wu Province.

sentences.zh: 及隋文帝執政，尉遲迥等舉兵，遠近騷然，人懷異望。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui took power, Yuchi Jiong and others raised troops; near and far were disturbed; people harbored divergent hopes.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui took power, Yuchi Jiong and others rose in arms; disturbance spread near and far, and people nursed divided loyalties.

sentences.zh: 顗自以族大，且為國家肺腑，懼文表圖己，謀欲先之。

translations.literal: Yan, considering himself of a great clan and being close kin to the imperial house, feared Wenbiao was plotting against him and planned to strike first.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yan, considering himself of a great clan and kin to the imperial house, feared Wenbiao meant to move against him and planned to strike first.

sentences.zh: 乃稱疾不出。

translations.literal: He therefore claimed illness and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and refused to leave his residence.

sentences.zh: 文表往問之，顗遂手刃文表。

translations.literal: Wenbiao went to inquire after him; Yan thereupon personally killed Wenbiao with a blade.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbiao went to visit him; Yu Yan then personally slew him.

sentences.zh: 因令吏人告云「文表謀反」，仍馳啟其狀。

translations.literal: He then had clerks and people report that "Wenbiao plotted rebellion," and immediately sent a fast dispatch stating the facts.
translations.idiomatic: He then had officials and townspeople report that Wenbiao had plotted rebellion and immediately sent an urgent dispatch to the throne.

sentences.zh: 隋文以諸方未定，恐顗為變，遂授顗吳州總管以安之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui, because the regions were not yet settled, feared Yan would rebel, and therefore granted Yan the post of governor-general of Wu Prefecture to reassure him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui, with the realm not yet settled, feared Yu Yan would turn rebel and granted him the post of governor-general of Wu Prefecture to reassure him.

sentences.zh: 後知文表無異志，雖不罪顗，而聽其子仁海襲爵。

translations.literal: Later, learning Wenbiao had no rebellious intent, though he did not punish Yan, he allowed his son Renhai to inherit the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Later, learning Wenbiao had borne no rebellious intent, he did not punish Yu Yan but allowed Wenbiao's son Renhai to inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The entire text uses the Zhonghua Shuju, November 1971 edition of the Book of Zhou, as the base for this collation.
translations.idiomatic: This text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the 《Book of Zhou》 (November 1971).
